These cutaneous signs are highly characteristic of dermatomyositis (DM).
- Presence of anti‑TIF‑1γ (p155) autoantibodies — a myositis‑specific autoantibody strongly associated with dermatomyositis and with striking cutaneous phenotypes. In adults it is associated with malignancy; in juveniles it is most often linked to JDM with prominent cutaneous disease.

- The combination of pathognomonic cutaneous stigmata (Gottron papules, shawl/V‑sign poikiloderma) plus anti‑TIF‑1γ makes dermatomyositis the overwhelmingly most likely diagnosis.
